---
title: "Path B · The Trainee"
subtitle: "From ODEs to a model you can defend in a viva"
---

**For:** graduate students, postdocs and academic modelers who need depth and a
defensible method, not just a working pipeline.

**Promise:** you understand what the estimation is doing, what the data can and
cannot identify, and how to quantify what you do not know.

**Ends at:** a reproducible, citable analysis with a DOI — something that counts
on a CV as well as in a job interview.

## Foundations — available now

| | Lesson | Emphasis for this path |
|---|---|---|

| 2 | [S0-01 · Compartments and ODEs](../lessons/s0-01-compartments-and-odes/index.qmd) | Derive rather than skim. Do the conditioning exercise in section 5 of the notebook |

| 5 | [S0-05 · Git for modelers](../lessons/s0-05-git-for-modelers/index.qmd) | Reproducibility is what makes the work citable |

optional here — academic groups usually have a stack already, and inheriting it
is the right default.

## The exercise that defines this path

`CASE-SM` publishes its true parameters. Use that properly, because you will
not get the opportunity again:

1. Fit the model and compare each estimate to the truth.
2. Ask *why* the miss is the size it is — design, variability, or identifiability.
3. Change the design (drop the rich day-14 profile, halve the subjects) and
   measure how the miss grows.

That third step is a study-design analysis, and it is the difference between
using a model and understanding one.

## What comes next

| Strand | On this path | Status |
|---|---|---|
| S1 · PK/PD core | Full depth, including TMDD and turnover models | planned |
| S2 · Population PK/PD | Estimation methods, covariate theory, evaluation | planned |
| S4 · QSP | Identifiability, sensitivity analysis, model reduction | planned |
| S5 · Bayes and ML | Priors, MCMC diagnostics, uncertainty quantification | planned |

Choose **one** of S3, S4 or S5 to go deep in. Depth is what a viva tests;
breadth is what a job interview tests, and it comes later and more easily.
